newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Iran seeks rail link with Bangladesh, Turkmenistan.
newsitem.headline: Iran seeks rail link with Bangladesh, Turkmenistan.

text.p: Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Alauddin Brujerdi said on Thursday that Iran, Turkmenistan and Bangladesh might develop rail transit link to ship goods.
"We have agreed on a tripartite issue between Turkmenistan, Iran and Bangladesh for transit of goods through rail communication," he told a news conference here.

Brujerdi arrived here on Tuesday on a three-day visit. He met Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad, Communications Minister Anwar Hossain and Shipping Minister A.S.M. Abdur Rab.
"We have discussed direct flights between Iran and Bangladesh with the communications minister," he said.
The Iranian minister also said the Afghan issue was important for peace in the region.
"Afghanistan requires a comprehensive government, otherwise tranquility will be hampered in the region," he said.
Brujerdi said he had handed a letter to Hasina from Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.
The Iranian president invited Hasina to visit his country and hoped for improved bilateral relations.
The president said Iran would permit many of the illegal Bangladeshi immigrants to stay in the country as a "gesture of goodwill for a brotherly country".
Brujerdi criticised the Organisation of the Islamic Conference for failing to take any concrete initiatives to solve the Afghan and Palestinian problems.
"It has failed miserably in solving the Moslem world's burning issues. The organisation is unable to solve the Afghanistan and Palestinian problems," he said.
